new.title: Explore world cultures at the MEG ethnography museum
new.desc: The Musée d'ethnographie de Genève was founded in 1901 under Eugène Pittard and holds about 100,000 objects from five continents. Since 31 October 2014 it has occupied a pagoda-shaped building on Boulevard Carl-Vogt.
new.tip: Permanent collection entry is cheap and the café is a good rest stop; allow two hours. Trams 12 and 15 stop at Plainpalais nearby.
new.q: Musée d'ethnographie de Genève MEG, Boulevard Carl-Vogt 65, Plainpalais, Genève

new.title: See Saussure's instruments at the science history museum
new.desc: The Musée d'histoire des sciences occupies the Villa Bartholoni, a neoclassical villa of the late 1820s on the lakeshore. It shows 17th to 19th century instruments from the cabinets of Geneva scholars such as de Saussure, Colladon and Pictet.
new.tip: Admission is free. Combine it with a walk through the Perle du Lac park next door.
new.q: Musée d'histoire des sciences, Rue de Lausanne 128, Pâquis, Genève

new.title: Picnic in the Parc de la Perle du Lac
new.desc: This lakeside park above Quai Wilson was named by Rolex founder Hans Wilsdorf's wife, who called it the pearl of the lake. The League of Nations bought part of the estate in 1926, and the park gives wide views of the lake and Mont Blanc.
new.tip: Come in late afternoon for the light on the water. Grilling is not allowed, but picnics are.
new.q: Parc de la Perle du Lac, Rue de Lausanne, Genève

new.title: Stroll Parc Mon Repos and its Plantamour villa
new.desc: Philippe Plantamour left the Mon Repos estate to the city on his death in 1898. The villa housed the ethnography museum from 1901 to 1939 and later served as the first home of Geneva television, which broadcast from here in 1954.
new.tip: The park is free and runs down to the lake. The old orangery now serves as a nature centre.
new.q: Parc Mon Repos, Rue de Lausanne, Pâquis, Genève

new.title: Watch the Rhône and Arve meet at the Jonction
new.desc: At the Pointe de la Jonction the clear Rhône and the grey, glacial Arve flow side by side before merging. The point lies at the western tip of the Plainpalais-Jonction district.
new.tip: Best on a sunny day when the colour difference is sharp. Do not swim here: the cold Arve water and strong currents are dangerous.
new.q: Pointe de la Jonction, Avenue de la Jonction, Genève

new.title: Admire the old hydro plant at the Bâtiment des Forces Motrices
new.desc: Engineer Théodore Turrettini built this hydroelectric plant on an island in the Rhône from 1883, with the main hall completed in 1892. It pumped water for Geneva's fountains and was listed as a monument in 1988 before reopening in 1997 as a theatre.
new.tip: The outside is best seen from the Pont de la Machine. Check the BFM programme for concerts and opera inside.
new.q: Bâtiment des Forces Motrices, Place des Volontaires 2, Genève

new.title: See a Gutenberg Bible at the Fondation Bodmer
new.desc: Martin Bodmer's library in Cologny holds about 150,000 items, among them a Gutenberg Bible, Greek papyri and Shakespeare first editions. Mario Botta designed the underground museum, which opened in 2003 and reopened with a redesigned display in September 2026.
new.tip: Book a ticket online and check the current opening days. Bus 33 or tram and bus from Rive reach Cologny.
new.q: Fondation Martin Bodmer, Route Martin-Bodmer 19, Cologny

new.title: Visit Voltaire's home at Les Délices
new.desc: Voltaire lived at Les Délices from 1755 to 1760 after leaving Prussia. The house now holds the Institut et Musée Voltaire, with his furniture, manuscripts and prints, set in the Parc des Délices.
new.tip: Entry to the museum is free. A monthly guided visit is offered in French.
new.q: Institut et Musée Voltaire, Rue des Délices 25, Genève

new.title: Find Calvin and Borges in the Cimetière des Rois
new.desc: Geneva's oldest cemetery dates from 1482 and is nicknamed the Genevan Pantheon. Calvin's simple marked grave lies here, as does the writer Jorge Luis Borges.
new.tip: Free entry during the day. Pick up the city's cemetery plan to find the graves.
new.q: Cimetière des Rois, Boulevard de la Cluse, Plainpalais, Genève

new.title: Trace the Reformation at the MIR museum
new.desc: The Musée international de la Réforme is in the 18th-century Maison Mallet, on the site of the old Saint-Pierre cloister where Geneva voted for the Reformation in 1536. Nine rooms trace its history in French, English and German.
new.tip: Open Tuesday to Sunday 10:00 to 17:00. It combines well with the cathedral towers next door.
new.q: Musée international de la Réforme, Cour Saint-Pierre 10, Genève

new.title: Sit on the 120 metre bench of the Promenade de la Treille
new.desc: The Treille bench is often called the longest wooden bench in the world at over 120 metres. Nearby grows the official chestnut tree whose first leaf, recorded by the city secretary since 1818, announces spring in Geneva.
new.tip: Bring a coffee from the Old Town and sit facing the Salève. Early evening is quietest.
new.q: Promenade de la Treille, Genève

new.title: Spot the Brunswick Monument on the quay
new.desc: Completed in 1879, this neo-Gothic marble mausoleum honours Charles II, Duke of Brunswick, who left his fortune to Geneva on condition it be built. It copies the Scaliger tombs of Verona.
new.tip: It stands on Quai du Mont-Blanc facing the Jet d'Eau. Visit at sunset for the lake view behind it.
new.q: Monument Brunswick, Quai du Mont-Blanc, Genève

new.title: Order oysters at the Café du Centre on Place du Molard
new.desc: This brasserie on the Place du Molard has been open since 1933 and is known as a seafood institution with oysters and shellfish platters. Its terrace sits on one of the oldest squares by the lake.
new.tip: Try oysters with a glass of Geneva white wine. Book for lunch on market days.
new.q: Café du Centre, Place du Molard 5, Genève

new.title: Share a fondue savièsarde at the Auberge de Savièse
new.desc: This chalet-style inn in the Pâquis serves several fondues and raclette in a wooden dining room. It is known for the Savièse-style fondue and a rare fondue chinoise.
new.tip: Book ahead, as it is always busy. Reasonably priced for central Geneva and open daily.
new.q: Auberge de Savièse, Rue des Pâquis 20, Genève

new.title: Taste Amandes Princesses at Auer chocolatier
new.desc: Auer is a family chocolatier founded in 1939 and now in its fifth generation. Its speciality is the Amande Princesse, a caramelised almond coated in milk chocolate and cocoa.
new.tip: Buy a small bag of the almonds and a few truffles. The shop is on Rue de Rive in the Rues Basses.
new.q: Auer Chocolatier, Rue de Rive 4, Genève

new.title: Buy a pavé de Genève at Chocolaterie Stettler
new.desc: Stettler & Castrischer is linked to the pavé de Genève, a cocoa-dusted chocolate cube filled with praline. The house dates to the 1940s and makes crunchy hazelnuts too.
new.tip: Take a box of pavés as a souvenir. The shop is on Rue du Rhône.
new.q: Chocolaterie Stettler, Avenue Blanc 49, Genève

new.title: Do a chocolate tasting at Favarger on Rue de Rive
new.desc: Favarger is one of Geneva's best-known chocolate houses, with a history going back to the 19th century. Its Rue de Rive shop offers a tasting plate through the city's Choco Pass.
new.tip: Open daily from late morning to early evening. Ask about the Choco Pass tasting plate.
new.q: Chocolats Favarger, Rue de Rive 11, Genève

new.title: Seek the hand-made pavé at Chocolats Rohr
new.desc: Rohr traces back to 1936 in Carouge and is described by the city's tourism office as the only firm still making pavés de Genève by hand to the original recipe. A shop sits on Place de Longemalle in the Rues Basses.
new.tip: Choose the classic pavé. Shops close early on Sundays, so go on a weekday.
new.q: Chocolats Rohr, Place de Longemalle, Genève

new.title: Pick pastries at Renou on Rue des Eaux-Vives
new.desc: Renou is a Geneva pâtisserie-chocolaterie led by pastry chef Christophe Renou, with shops in Carouge, Plan-les-Ouates and the city. The Rue des Eaux-Vives shop sells fine tarts, viennoiseries and chocolates.
new.tip: Open weekdays; arrive early for fresh croissants. The shop closes for a midday break.
new.q: Renou Genève Pâtisserie Chocolaterie, Rue des Eaux-Vives 2, Genève

new.title: Eat longeole and lentils at La Bise in Carouge
new.desc: La Bise cooks from fresh regional products and a Swiss-only wine list. The menu has featured IGP Longeole, Geneva's aniseed pork sausage, with green lentils.
new.tip: Open Tuesday to Saturday evenings. Book a table in the cold months when longeole is in season.
new.q: La Bise, Rue Roi-Victor Amé 8, Carouge

new.title: Order choucroute at Brasserie Lipp
new.desc: The Geneva branch of the Paris brasserie opened in 1986 in the Confédération Centre. Its menu centres on choucroute, cassoulet, steaks and seafood in a busy art-deco-style room.
new.tip: Choucroute is the dish to order. Open late, so it works for a post-theatre meal.
new.q: Brasserie Lipp, Rue de la Confédération 8, Genève

new.title: Have a coffee and ice cream at Café Remor
new.desc: Café Remor on Place du Cirque is a local favourite near the Jonction, with a history going back to about 1920 as a glacier and tea room.
new.tip: Try the house ice cream or a morning coffee with a croissant. Popular with locals at weekends.
new.q: Café Remor, Place du Cirque 3, Genève

new.title: Eat a Lebanese mezze at Parfums de Beyrouth
new.desc: This Pâquis restaurant serves traditional Lebanese specialities and is often called a pillar of the neighbourhood's night-time dining. The Pâquis is Geneva's most international quarter for cheap, varied food.
new.tip: Order a mezze spread to share with grilled skewers and aubergine dip. Open late.
new.q: Parfums de Beyrouth, Rue de Berne 18, Genève

new.title: Visit the free animal park in the Bois de la Bâtie
new.desc: At the top of the Bois de la Bâtie hill, the city runs a free animal park with regional wildlife, farmyard animals and old Swiss breeds, part of ProSpecieRara conservation programmes. A large playground and paddling pool are close by.
new.tip: Free and open daily. Bus 2 or 19 to Clair-Vue; dogs and cats are not allowed.
new.q: Parc aux animaux du Bois de la Bâtie, Chemin de la Bâtie 28, Petit-Lancy

new.title: Walk the Rhône banks from the Jonction
new.desc: The city describes a walk along the Rhône through Plainpalais-Jonction, past old pontoons, swimming spots and the confluence with the Arve. It runs between the Jonction and the central bridges.
new.tip: Follow the left-bank path towards the BFM. Swim only in the zone signed by the city, never near the Arve.
new.q: Bords du Rhône, Quai du Cheval-Blanc, Jonction, Genève

new.title: Catch a film at the Black Movie festival in January
new.desc: Black Movie is an international independent film festival that ran its 27th edition from 16 to 25 January 2026, with around a hundred films. It also has a children's programme.
new.tip: Buy tickets per screening on the festival site. Venues are central.
new.q: Maison des arts du Grütli, Rue du Général-Dufour 16, Genève

new.title: Browse Noël au Quai on the lakefront
new.desc: Geneva's main Christmas market, Noël au Quai, runs on Quai du Mont-Blanc and is free to enter. In 2026 it is planned from 19 November to 24 December.
new.tip: Come on a weekday evening to avoid crowds. About ten minutes from Cornavin station.
new.q: Noël au Quai, Quai du Mont-Blanc, Genève

new.title: Skate on the Bastions outdoor rink
new.desc: Each winter the city sets up a seasonal rink in the Parc des Bastions near the Reformation Monument. Entry is free, with skate hire at CHF 2 last season, and themed disco evenings.
new.tip: Last season ran from late November to 1 March. Check dates on the city's rink page.
new.q: Patinoire des Bastions, Parc des Bastions, Genève

new.title: Watch a free open-air film at CinéTransat
new.desc: CinéTransat is a free outdoor cinema on the lawn of the Parc de la Perle du Lac, with a giant screen, a bar and a short Swiss film before each feature. The 2026 season ran from 9 July to 17 August.
new.tip: Bring a blanket or folding chair. Screenings are cancelled for rain or wind, announced by 19:00.
new.q: CinéTransat, Parc de la Perle du Lac, Genève

new.title: Hear the Orchestre de la Suisse Romande at Victoria Hall
new.desc: The 1,700-seat Victoria Hall was given to the city in 1901 and is home to the Orchestre de la Suisse Romande, founded by Ernest Ansermet in 1918. Gandhi spoke here in December 1931.
new.tip: Check the OSR season programme and book ahead; last-minute youth tickets are often cheap.
new.q: Victoria Hall, Rue du Général-Dufour 14, Genève
